newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares hit record high.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares hit record high.

text.p: Leading Russian shares hit a record on Thursday despite fluctuating in midday trading on scattered profit taking, traders said.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed up almost three percent at 388.99 after closing at 377.69 on Wednesday.

Nikolai Fomintsev, head of securities at East-European Investment Company, forecast possible early gains on Friday, but he said profit-taking could strike again in LUKoil and other leading shares, which have gained in recent days.
"Tomorrow, buying will continue, but how it will be around 12 or one o'clock is difficult to say," he said.
National energy monopoly UES rose to finish the day at $0.3270 from Wednesday's close $0.3244 but off a daily high of $0.3345. Regional power company Mosenergo jumped to $1.414 from $1.367.
Oil company LUKoil rose to $17.25 from $16.80 but was off its earlier high in the day of $17.47.

Centreinvest Securities' head of strategic investment, Alexander Babayan, said the market remained strong on active Western and domestic interest and said demand in Russia's Far Eastern companies was especially big.
"Those investors that have been in the market for a long time are looking at small undervalued companies -- Primorsky shipping -- all the shipping companies," said Babayan.
"You don't see a lot of trading going on on the screen, but there's a buying frenzy going in that region."
Fomintsev attributed the Russian market's rise to high Dow Jones index levels on the eve of a forthcoming U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on interest rates.
